data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Ownership does not suppress discovery but delays it, and the evidence is a monotonic increase in solution latency across a sequence of similar problems.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Solution latency remains constant or decreases over time, indicating no delay cost.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Rival lineages solve problems instantly that the owner cannot solve at all, proving structural suppression rather than delay.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The sequence of problems is not similar enough to allow learning curve effects.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Exclusive ownership forces a lineage to re-invent concepts that rivals already possess. This is a latency penalty, not a discovery failure. The lineage will eventually find the explanation, but later than a rival would have. To distinguish suppression from efficiency, count the time-to-solution for the owning lineage. If the time-to-solution increases or fails to decrease as expected on similar problems, the system is paying an increasing efficiency penalty, which functionally suppresses timely cross-cutting explanations.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
